title: SPA/672/2017 of Manmodh Singh Vs Dinesh Singh AND OTHERS

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
(Delay Condonation Application No.11277 of 2017)
In
Special Appeal No.672 of 2017
Manmodh Singh .ÖAppellant
Versus
Dinesh Singh & others .ÖRespondents
Mr. Amar Shukla, Advocate holding brief of Mr. Shivanand Bhatt,
Advocate for the appellant.
Mr. Shiv Pande, Advocate for respondent no.1.
Mr. Anil Kumar Bisht, Standing Counsel for the State of
Uttarakhand/respondent nos.2 to 4.
 Dated: 26.10.2017
Coram: Honíble K.M. Joseph, C.J.
 Honíble V.K. Bist, J.
K.M. Joseph, C.J (Oral)
 There is delay of 94 days in filing the appeal.
According to the appellant, the delay was occasioned
because of the reason that in the original judgment, the
appellant had no reason to feel aggrieved. It is only after
the correction was carried out, the appellant found it
necessary to challenge it. Though there is objection filed
to the delay condonation application, we are of the view
that delay should be condoned. Accordingly, the delay is
condoned. The application for condonation of delay is
allowed.
2. The appellant is the 4th respondent in the writ
petition. The facts, which are not in dispute are that on
24.08.2014 an advertisement was issued for appointment
to the post of Junior Clerk in an Inter College, which is
an aided institution. 38 persons applied out of which, 26
applications were found correct. The appellant after the
interview was selected. Thereafter, two writ petitions were

2
filed; one by the present writ petitioner and another by
his father-in-law, who was the then Principal. The
judgment in the said writ petitions has been produced as
Annexure No.4 to the writ petition. The Court took the
view that as far as petition filed by the Principal, who was
the relative of the other writ petitioner is concerned, the
same could not have been maintained and the said writ
petition, namely, Writ Petition (S/S) No.332 of 2015 filed
by the Principal was dismissed. The petition filed by the
present petitioner was also dismissed. The dismissal of
the writ petition filed by the Principal was subjected to
one caveat, namely, that in case there is a complaint with
regard to the present appellant, who was respondent no.6
in that writ petition, that false certificate has been given,
then his candidature should be rejected. In paragraph 13
of the common judgment, the following was the
observations:-
ì13. Let the same be examined by the
Chief Education Officer and in case he is
satisfied with the certificate, its genuine
and bona fide, he shall forthwith give
appointment to respondent no.6. In case,
the authority concerned finds any
anomaly regarding the said document, he
shall proceed afresh, in accordance with
law, to fill up the said post.î
3. According to the appellant, thereafter the Chief
Education Officer examined the matter and passed order
dated 12.01.2016. It was found that the documents of
the appellant are genuine and direction was given to the
Principal of the College to give joining to the appellant, as
the Principal was not giving joining. It is thereafter that
the present writ petition was filed and the writ petition
has been allowed by the impugned judgment dated
03.05.2017 which reads as follows:-

3
ìPetitioner participated in the selection
process for the post of Assistant Teacher in Inter
College Kotalgaon (Bhatura) District Tehri
Garhwal. The appointment letter was not issued
to the petitioner since the genuineness of the
experience certificate furnished by the petitioner
was in question. Petitioner approached this Court
by way of WPSS No.332 of 2015. It was disposed
of on 3.11.2015. A direction was issued to the
Chief Education Officer to re-examine the
genuineness of the experience certificate supplied
by the petitioner.
However, surprisingly, the Chief Education
Officer, by its order dated 12.1.2016, without re-examining the issue, has reiterated the earlier
stand contrary to the directions issued by this
Court on 3.11.2015.
Accordingly, the petition is allowed. Order
dated 12.1.2016 is quashed and set aside. The
concerned Chief Education Officer is directed to
decide the issue of genuineness of experience
certificate furnished by the petitioner in
conformity with the order dated 3.11.2015
passed by this Court in WPSS No.332 of 2015
within eight weeks from today.
All pending applications stand disposed of
in the above terms.î
4. Mr. Amar Shukla, learned counsel for the
appellant, would complain that in the writ petition there
was no relief sought to challenge the order dated
12.01.2016 and yet the said order has been quashed.
Furthermore, he would submit that in the earlier round,
the writ petition filed by the present writ petitioner was
dismissed and he has no right to challenge the order, as
infact, he was the person, who was found not eligible to
be considered for appointment. Therefore, the petition
was not maintainable.
5. Mr. Shiv Pande, Advocate for respondent no.1/
writ petitioner would submit that pursuant to the earlier
judgment, a contempt was filed. Pursuant to the order

4
passed in the contempt, a fresh order has been passed by
the Chief Education Officer, which is infact, in favour of
the appellant. There is a case for the writ petitioner that
Chief Education Officer was hand in glove with the
appellant. Even the order of the Chief Education Officer
is not challenged and there is no scope of even examining
such contention.
6. After hearing the learned counsel for the
parties, certain facts cannot be in the region of doubt.
The earlier writ petition filed by the present writ
petitioner had been dismissed. As noted, the writ petition
filed by the father-in-law of the writ petitioner was also
dismissed subject to the caveat and the observation,
which we have already extracted. Apparently, the Chief
Education Officer has passed the order dated
12.01.2016. That order has not specifically been called in
question in the present writ petition. Furthermore, the
present writ petition was filed by the candidate, who was,
infact, found not eligible to be considered. Lastly, fresh
order has been passed pursuant to the proceedings in
contempt, which also is in favour of the appellant.
7. Having regard to all these aspects, we find that
the learned Single Judge was not justified in granting the
relief as granted in the writ petition. Therefore, the appeal
is only to be allowed. The appeal will stand allowed. The
writ petition will stand dismissed. No order as to costs.
 (V.K. Bist, J.) (K.M. Joseph, C.J.)
 26.10.2017
